hypothesis_text: On altcoin perpetual futures (alt_theme basket), persistently elevated positive 7-day cumulative funding rates (z-score > 1.2) reflect crowded speculative long positioning where longs pay substantial carry financing to shorts. When this crowded carry meets aggressive taker selling pressure (taker_buy_ratio_1h < 0.48, gate_low) amid high open interest leverage accumulation (oi_change_pct_4h gate_high), speculative longs suffer margin fatigue and liquidation cascade vulnerability, causing price mean-reversion over 1h to 4h horizons.
narrative: In cryptocurrency perpetual futures markets, funding rates act as an equilibrating mechanism transferring carry cost between long and short contract holders every 8 hours. When speculative enthusiasm pushes altcoin funding rates to persistent extremes over a 7-day trailing window (z-score > 1.2), long open interest absorbs continuous negative carry cash flow. In isolation, a high funding rate can persist if upward spot momentum continues to exceed the carry drag. However, when aggressive market participants begin hitting bids (taker_buy_ratio_1h < 0.48 / gate_low), the momentum engine halts. Simultaneously, when open interest has expanded over the preceding 4-hour window (oi_change_pct_4h gate_high), leverage in the system is maximized and long positions are held with tight liquidation margins. As taker selling initiates localized downward price slippage, overleveraged longs face adverse margin calls and forced de-leveraging. The resulting order flow becomes one-sided liquidation selling and inventory rebalancing by market makers, forcing prices lower over 1h, 2h, and 4h horizons.
research_rationale: Anchor candidate XL_LINKUSDT_bcbc36990472 was locked on LINKUSDT from the bounded expression_lab evaluation of funding_rate_zscore_7d > 1.2 combined with taker_buy_ratio_1h < 0.48. On the 430-day scan panel, this condition matches 7,637 bars across 1,968 episodes and 164 independent active days, showing healthy cross-sectional distribution across all 8 alt_theme symbols (ranging from 32 to 79 events per symbol; LINKUSDT has 60 events). T1 event-based scoring projects 1,129 observations at 60m, 785 at 120m, and 504 at 240m, safely clearing the 250-observation certification floor. Regarding prior knowledge and ledger evidence: (1) taker_buy_ratio_1h with gate_low directly follows the market structure prior in gene_knowledge (carry_unwind trigger: opposite_side with confidence sufficient, n=36, shrink_weight=0.643). The cemetery indicates taker_buy_ratio_1h with min had 2 T1 survival passes out of 33 trials (top kill was T1.20-REGIME-FILTER), whereas unconditioned gate_opposite_side suffered evidential kills from noise. By formulating the condition as a locked expression_gate combined with gate_low, we isolate true exhaustion selling. (2) oi_change_pct_4h with gate_high follows the prior table for exposure (leverage expansion, confidence insufficient_data, n=18, shrink_weight=0.474), ensuring positions are levered and vulnerable to unwind. (3) volume_ratio_1h with gate_tail is an exploratory absorption partner (confidence untested) designed to filter out low-liquidity bars and ensure sufficient turnover during the unwind. Addressing cemetery dominant kill codes: The anchor gene funding_rate_zscore_7d has 694 historical trials in the cemetery with 5 T1 survivals, where the dominant kill code was T0.04-IC-STAT (579 trials) due to continuous dense signal dilution across uncrowded periods. Our design explicitly overcomes T0.04-IC-STAT by using an event-gated locked predicate (funding_rate_zscore_7d > 1.2 and taker_buy_ratio_1h < 0.48) that only activates during confirmed carry crowding and selling pressure. Furthermore, horizon analysis in the cemetery confirms that 1h (4 survivals) and 2h (1 survival) horizons are viable, while 30m and 4h had zero survivals; our predicted band [1h, 2h, 4h] aligns directly with these empirical horizon dynamics.
